To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sum-connectivity is the unique t-index for which the star is the minimizer over all connected graphs, and the path is the unique t -index for which the path is the maximizer over all trees.

the star is the minimum-degree graph for the sum-connectivity and several other topological indices, and the path and cycle maximize the sum-connectivity, the Wiener index and several other topologies.

the star and path are the unique graphs minimizing and maximizing the sum-connectivity (or more general) index over trees and unicyclical graphs, respectively, and that the quasi-tree consisting of an n -vertex cycle with chords to c consecutive vertices is the unique quasi-tree maximizing the index.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the extremal problems for t -indices, where the edge-weight function t satisfies the conditions in each of the problems.
the extremal properties of the t -index for various classes of graphs.
extremal problems for a family of degree-based topological graph invariants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the star is the only n -vertex graph minimizing the t-index over graphs with no isolated vertex, and the only n -cycle plus some chords maximizing it over quasi-trees, when the conditions on t are satisfied.

for a decreasing function t satisfying the above conditions, the star minimizes the t -index among connected graphs, the path maximizes the t - index among trees, the cycle among unicyclic graphs, and the n -vertex graph obtained from an n -cycle by adding chords to some number c vertices maximizes the t-index among quasi-trees, where c is a function of n and the conditions imposed on the function t.
, for the sum-connectivity (and more general) indices, the star is a unique minimum, and the path/cycle and a quasi-tree with one cycle plus chords are unique maximums.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for the sum-connectivity and other indices satisfying our conditions, the extremal problems are solved.
the star is always a minimizer, and the path and cycle always maximizers, of the t -index.
the extremal graphs are always trees, cycles or stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sum-connectivity is the most well-behaved edge-weight index.
the extremal properties of the sum-connectivity and Wiener index are not shared by other degree-based indices.
extremal results for the t -indices of graphs can be established by considering the t -index of trees and quasi-trees, and by exploiting properties of t ( z ).
